title: Health review of CodeAlta
scope: whole repository at `feature50`: .NET libraries and executables, desktop frontend, tests, CI, docs and agent instructions
verdict: The core rules hold: one writer per session, clean low layers, guardrail tests that catch regressions. The cost is in how state is saved and decisions repeated: stores whose saves their readers refuse, provider edits that bypass the store's lock, decisions kept in two places, and one 6,700-line component every feature edits. Most cures delete or merge code.

findings.title: Keep the automation state within the size its own reader accepts
findings.claim: The automation state can be saved larger than the 8 MiB its reader accepts; the next start then loads empty state with every automation paused, no run history and no trigger watermarks.

evidence.text: A try records each call it does not make, as a line of up to 2,000 characters.
Up to 50 such calls per run.
100 runs kept per automation, 2,000 in all, against a reader limit of 8 MiB: one automation alone can reach 10 MB.
Retention counts runs, not bytes.
The reader returns nothing above the limit and marks the file unreadable; the store then starts empty and paused.
The paused, empty state that replaces it.
`Save` writes the whole state whatever its size.

findings.change: Make the read limit a rule of the save: when the serialized state is over budget, drop the oldest completed runs, their calls first, until it fits. Never drop runs in progress, the pause choice, approvals or trigger watermarks; if those alone do not fit, fail the save and keep the last readable file.

removes: the outcome where a save succeeds and the next start loses the state of every automation
adds: a size check on the bytes already serialized
one round-trip test

items.label: next start keeps state and pause choice

findings.firstStep: A test that fills a state just under 8 MiB, adds one run that crosses the limit and reopens the store: today it starts paused and empty. Then the size check in `Save`.
verify: The reopened store keeps the newest run and a watermark set before, and stays unpaused.
The automation tests of `CodeAlta.Desktop.Tests` pass; the test of a malformed file still pauses.
risks: The limits on runs become upper bounds: 100 very large runs may not all be kept.
findings.ifNot: A user who runs long tries of many automations finds them all paused one morning, with their history and trigger state gone.

findings.title: Grant an automation occurrence only once its claim is written
findings.claim: When the claim file cannot be written, `TryClaim` still grants the occurrence; after a restart the claim is gone and the same occurrence can be granted and run a second time.

evidence.text: `TryClaim` saves, then returns true whatever the save did.
`Save` swallows I/O and access errors.
An unreadable claim file reads as no claims at all.
The grant reaches the start of the run.
Commit `09ee9a3ef` fixed the same assumption for the hourly call counter, whose store now returns the result of its save.

findings.change: `Save` returns whether it wrote, and `TryClaim` grants only then. An unreadable ledger means "storage unavailable", not "no claims": the scheduler skips or defers the occurrence with that reason.

removes: a grant that no file records
the reading of an I/O error as an absence
adds: a claim outcome
an error-path test

findings.firstStep: In the placement fixture, make the claim file unwritable and check that the start is refused; keep the restart test that passes today.
verify: Zero runner starts on a failed claim write.
After the storage recovers, a reopened store refuses the same occurrence.
risks: A missed or deferred occurrence is preferred to a duplicate run: a pooled event must not be marked seen when its claim failed.
findings.ifNot: Rare, but when it happens the side effects of an automation run twice.

findings.title: Edit the providers of `config.toml` through the store's locked update, on the raw definitions
findings.claim: Thirteen call sites in the desktop, the node and the TUI read and rewrite the whole provider list of `config.toml` by themselves: none holds the file lock from the read to the write, so two writers from one revision both succeed and one edit is lost; and the model-server and node paths read the definitions with their defaults filled in, which wrote an implicit `api_url` into an untouched, disabled llama.cpp provider.

evidence.text: The store already has a read-and-save under the lock of the file, which nine settings writers use and no provider edit does.
The callers of `UpdateGlobal`: settings only.
The 13 callers of the whole-list save, outside the store (the 14th line of this search is the store's own declaration).
The text editor holds the file lock across its revision check and its save.
The structured form checks the revision under an in-process lock only; the store takes the file lock at the save.
Adding a model server reads the completed definitions and saves them all back.
That read fills in the defaults of every definition.
The node does the same for the providers of a scope.
The form avoids it on purpose: "no defaults are filled in, so saving them back adds none".

findings.change: Give the store one provider edit: under `ConfigFileLock`, read the raw definitions, apply the caller's change, check the revision when the caller has one, save. Move the 14 call sites to it, the model-server and node paths first. Complete the definitions only to apply them to the runtime, after the write.

removes: 14 hand-written read-modify-write loops
defaults written into untouched providers
edits lost between two writers (the developer instance shares `config.toml`)
adds: one store method of about 20 lines
a two-writer test and a raw round-trip test

items.label: read: completed or raw, each its own
the store's provider edit
items.note: lock, raw read, edit, revision, save

findings.firstStep: Add the store method and move the model-server path to it, with a test: a config with an untouched, disabled llama.cpp provider gets no `api_url` when a model server is added, and an unknown provider section stays as it is.
steps: Move the structured form and check two writers on one revision: one `ok`, one `conflict`.
Move the TUI coordinator; the whole-list save remains for the store only.
verify: No caller outside the store reads completed definitions to save them.
The two-writer test returns exactly one `ok`, and the winner's value is on disk.
risks: `ConfigFileLock` is a thread-affine mutex: the edit must not span an `await`.
Disabled providers and providers of an unknown type stay as they are.
findings.ifNot: Each new caller copies one of the 14 loops, and an edit made in the developer instance while the normal one saves is lost without a word.

findings.claim: Saving one provider in the TUI rewrites every provider through a private copier that lacks seven properties the store's copy keeps, so it removes them from untouched providers in `config.toml`.

evidence.text: The TUI copier: no `ContextSize`, `Sandbox`, `CodeMode`, `Server`, `Request`, `ModelRequest` or `Headers`.
The store's copy, which has them.
The dialog rebuilds every provider to save.
The merge removes the modeled keys a definition no longer has.
Commit `77da0870b` had to add the model visibility rules to both copies; a third copier exists for documents.

findings.change: Use `CodeAltaConfigStore.CloneProviderDefinition` in both paths of the TUI editor and delete its copier.

removes: a 64-line copier and its own list of fields
adds: one preservation test

findings.firstStep: Extend the round trip of `ProviderFrontendCoordinatorTests` with an untouched provider that has a `server` and a `context_size`: it fails today. Then replace the copier.
verify: The untouched provider keeps both settings when the config is reopened.
The tests of omitted defaults still pass.
risks: The store's copy deep-copies nested tables: compare values, not references.
findings.ifNot: A TUI user who renames one provider loses the model server or the sandbox of another.

findings.title: Add the missing columns of the session list at each open, from one list
findings.claim: Three times in six days a column added to the session list broke listing sessions on every existing database ("no such column"), because its migration only runs when `SchemaVersion` changes and the version was not raised.

evidence.text: The migration is skipped when the stored version is the one asked for.
The version of the session list.
Nine hand-written `Add…ColumnAsync` methods, each a `pragma_table_info` check then an `ALTER TABLE`.
Three fixes that only raised the version: sandbox column ("no such column: c.local_sandbox"), options column, cloud column.
Every new fact about sessions is a column or a table of the database.

findings.change: Declare each column once: name, type, and whether adding it invalidates the rows. At each open, read `pragma_table_info` (a read) and add what is missing in one write. Keep `SchemaVersion` for what a list of columns cannot express: moving large values, dropping a column.

removes: nine near-identical methods, about 170 lines
the rule "raise the version when you add a column"
adds: a column table and a loop of about 30 lines

items.label: add the column to the list

findings.firstStep: A test that creates the session tables without one declared column, at the current version, then lists sessions: it fails today. Then the loop; the nine methods go.
verify: That test passes, also for a column added to the list without changing the version.
`CodeAlta.Catalog.Tests` pass.
risks: The permission-mode and space columns also clear the rows: keep that flag per column.
An up-to-date database must stay a read at open (`ApplicationDatabase.cs:337`).
findings.ifNot: The next column of a session breaks the session list of every user who already has a database.
findings.dissent: One analyst would keep the version gate and add a test that opens a fixture of the last shipped schema at its real version, refreshed with each release. It catches a missed bump; the column list removes the bump itself and the nine methods, for one read of `pragma_table_info` at open. Kept: the column list.

findings.title: Give Settings the inherited project scope that sessions use
findings.claim: For a sub-project, Settings and the session disagree on skills, prompts and plugins: a repository skill offered to the session is missing from Settings, a skill the parent turned off shows as on, and the Prompts and Plugins pages show the sub-project's own entries only, against the user guide.

evidence.text: A session takes the inherited roots, the effective folders and the disabled names of every ancestor.
The Settings listing reads the sub-project's disabled names only, with one root.
Its query: one project root.
The page passes `SkillFolders`, not `EffectiveSkillFolders`.
The scope of a Settings page is resolved to a root only, for every page.
The Prompts page queries that root alone.
What the user guide says a sub-project inherits.

findings.change: `SettingsProjectScope.ResolveAsync` returns the project, and the Skills, Prompts and Plugins pages read through the computation of effective roots and disabled names that sessions use (`ProjectResourceRoots.Inherited`). Settings keeps its diagnostics; creating, deleting and configuring still write to the sub-project's own files.

removes: a second definition of what a sub-project inherits, in three pages
adds: a sub-project fixture per page

findings.firstStep: Skills: carry the parent's disabled names into the listing of a sub-project, with a test where a user skill is turned off by the parent only.
steps: Prompts, then Plugins, through the same resolved project.
verify: The sub-project lists that skill as unavailable; a skill of the parent is listed and offered.
Prompts and Plugins of a sub-project list the repository's entries, read-only.
risks: An inherited entry stays read-only from the sub-project: a repository-level off must not become a setting of the sub-project.
findings.ifNot: In a monorepo, Settings keeps showing a list the sessions do not use.

findings.title: Let a desktop RPC service declare its JSON types and fixtures in its own file
findings.claim: A new RPC service edits its own file and five shared ones; `BootRpc.cs` changed in 109 commits in four weeks, all in its list of 1,021 `[JsonSerializable]` lines, and `demo-api.ts` in 45, 38 of them with `BootRpc.cs`.

evidence.text: The labels service: its file, `DesktopApplication.cs` (twice), `BootRpc.cs`, `demo-api.ts` and a fixture.
One context for every RPC type of the desktop.
NeoAstra is given that one context type.
A stub of `unavailable` methods per service.
A fixture that names 60 services one by one, and chooses some on purpose (the demo `reminder`, not the shell fixture's).

findings.change: Each `*Rpc.cs` declares `partial class DesktopJsonContext` with the attributes of its own types, if the JSON source generator accepts them spread over partial declarations: the first step tells. In `demo-api.ts`, a service whose every method answers `unavailable` is built by one helper; the fixtures keep their explicit choices. With F10, the second registration in `DesktopApplication.cs` goes too.

removes: the central list of 1,021 attributes
the stub methods of the services the demo does not fake
adds: one partial declaration per RPC file
one stub helper

findings.firstStep: Move the attributes of one RPC file (`ReleaseNotesRpc.cs`) to a partial declaration in that file; build and run its RPC tests.
verify: `BootRpc.cs` holds the boot types only.
A new service edits its own file, `DesktopApplication.cs` and `main.tsx`, nothing else.
risks: A type shared by two services is declared once.
The demo answers some reads with empty data on purpose (`labels.list`): those stay explicit.
findings.dissent: One analyst proposed one JSON context per RPC file, combined at start: `[assembly: NeoRpcJsonContext(typeof(DesktopJsonContext))]` names a single context for NeoAstra, so the partial declarations are the cure kept. Another showed that `export *` in the fixtures would lose the choices they make on purpose: they stay explicit. Landing showed that the System.Text.Json source generator refuses `[JsonSerializable]` spread over partial declarations: `CS8785`, "The hintName 'DesktopJsonContext.Boolean.g.cs' of the added source file must be unique within a generator". With NeoAstra taking one context, `BootRpc.cs` keeps its list until NeoAstra accepts several.

findings.title: Remove the early return that drops the credential policies of the `alta` commands
findings.claim: The built-in commands test about 20 optional services twice, once to build the commands and once to list their policies, and the two lists have drifted: a credential broker alone enables the `credential` commands, but the early return of the policies does not test it and skips their policies.

evidence.text: A broker alone adds the `credential` commands.
The early return lists 20 services but not the broker.
The credential policies come after it.
The registry treats the built-in contributor as one type for its allowlists: splitting it is not free.

findings.change: Delete the early return, so the policies follow the same tests as the commands; the cost is one list copy when no service is there.

adds: one test of a host with the broker alone

findings.firstStep: A test with only the credential broker registered asserts that the `credential` policies are listed: it fails today. Then the credentials contributor.
verify: The test passes; the help and policy tests of `AltaLiveToolTests` pass.

findings.dissent: The analyst who found it proposed one contributor per domain; the registry recognizes the built-in contributor by its type (`AltaCommandRegistry.cs:49`, `:141`), so the split was left for when that code changes. Kept: the one-line fix.

findings.title: Move the state of features out of the `App` component
findings.claim: `App` in `main.tsx` is one component of 6,741 lines with 134 `useState`, 95 `useEffect` and 94 `useRef`; 144 commits changed `main.tsx` in four weeks (22.7 files each on average), and four text fields re-render the whole window at each keystroke, against the development guide.

evidence.text: The component, from line 550 to line 7291.
Keystrokes of the sidebar filter set state of `App`.
The project rename field.
The session rename field.
The Settings search.
The state of the rename, delete and move of sessions and projects, held by `App`.
"Keystrokes, tokens and timers never re-render the whole app".
A tab switch renders all of `App`: "a gain needs the whole of `App` not to render for a switch".
144 commits in four weeks.

findings.change: Each field keeps its own draft: the rename popover the title it edits, the project rename its name, the sidebar filter its text, the Settings overlay its search; they pass the value on submit. The busy and conflict state stays with the mutation, which the sidebar also reads. Then move, one per commit, the dialogs whose state no other surface reads. `App` keeps what the window shares: the workspace, the tabs, the selection.

removes: about 40 `useState` and their effects from `App` in the first steps
whole-window renders while typing
adds: a component or a hook per surface, in folders that exist

findings.firstStep: `RenamePopover` keeps the title it edits and calls back on submit; `renamingTitle` leaves `App`. A browser test counts the renders of `App` while typing a title.
steps: The project rename, then the sidebar filter and the Settings search.
The dialogs whose state no other surface reads, one per commit.
Measure the tab switch again (task `wtvm`) before choosing an external store.
verify: No render of `App` per keystroke in the rename popover, the sidebar filter and the Settings search.
`npm test` passes; the count of `useState` in `App` falls at each step.
risks: State two surfaces read (selection, workspace) stays shared.
Moved effects stay idempotent under StrictMode.
findings.dissent: The analysts differ on the order: the smallest surfaces first, Settings first, or the drafts only. Settled: the drafts first (one field, one test each); the busy state stays where the sidebar reads it; larger moves only once the drafts are out.

findings.title: Keep the tracked files in the fallback snapshot of a review, and say why the first attempt failed
findings.claim: When the first snapshot of a review fails, the fallback starts from an empty index and runs `git add -A`, so a tracked file under an ignore rule drops out of the tree and an approval can miss its edit; and the first failure loses its reason, as on a Windows CI run (43251505041).

evidence.text: The fallback writes the tree without the copy of the real index.
The real index is copied only when a seed is given; then `git add -A` adds what is not ignored.
A tracked file under an ignore rule, in the repository's own fixture.
An approval holds while the tree of the work tree equals the approved snapshot.
Git's errors and the I/O exceptions are discarded.
The assertion that failed on CI, before anything is held.

findings.change: The fallback starts from the tracked set (for example `git read-tree HEAD`) instead of an empty index, so both attempts hash the same files. Each failed stage (`add`, `write-tree`, an exception) keeps its reason for the log and the test; the public result stays nullable.

removes: a fallback that can approve a different tree
a failure without a reason
adds: one step to the fallback
a reason on the internal result

findings.firstStep: Extend the equality check of `ReviewServiceTests` with the fixture of a tracked file under an ignore rule: through the fallback it is missing today.
verify: Both attempts give the same tree for that fixture.
A failure of this test on CI names the failed stage and git's error.
risks: The reason may hold paths: keep it out of what the user sees.
findings.ifNot: On a machine whose antivirus holds the index copy, a review can approve a tree that lacks the edit of a tracked, ignored file.

healthy.title: One writer per session
healthy.note: The pending model and prompt of a session are written inside `actor.QueryAsync` (`SessionRuntimeService.cs:1442-1457`): the size of `SessionRuntimeService` does not come with writes outside its actor.

healthy.title: Guardrail tests and the low layers
healthy.note: `ArchitectureGuardrailTests` of the desktop and the server, and the node's guardrails, keep `CodeAlta.Core`, `CodeAlta.CodeMode`, `CodeAlta.Search` and the fleet protocol free of the layers above.

healthy.title: One source of test time
healthy.note: `TestTime` and `testLimit`, with `WithinAsync` naming what was awaited: none of the failures found on CI was a timeout.

healthy.title: The locks of the configuration
healthy.note: `ConfigFileLock` and `UpdateGlobal` already give a locked read-and-save of `config.toml`; F03 moves the provider edits onto them, no new lock.

dropped.title: Give `CodeModeRunRegistry` the clock of its store
dropped.reason: The CI failure it explained was a race with the writes of a stopped run, fixed by `f535964b9` the next day; the clock cannot make the wake time null.

dropped.title: Check what an agent does through one path instead of at each command
dropped.reason: The checks at each command need what only the parsed command knows: the resolved MCP tool, the plugin's policy, the lineage of the target session. Security is also outside the scope of this review.

dropped.title: Select the platform tests by `[TestClass]` or a test category because helper names enter the filter
dropped.reason: The helper names match no test: the filter is `FullyQualifiedName~.<Name>.`, and no test name has such a segment.

dropped.title: Mask secrets once, at the publish and journal boundary of `AgentSession`
dropped.reason: Rejected in review: the events of a session are already masked before its history, its journal and its publication (`AgentSession.cs:3479`); the other call sites feed a summary or a permission callback, which one sink cannot replace. Security is also outside the scope of this review.

dropped.title: Group the 63 host options into records with presets per host
dropped.reason: `f411ce863` moved the drifted defaults into the host; grouping adds types without a defect that remains, and the desktop registration part is in F07 and F10.

dropped.title: Split `SessionRuntimeService` (16,037 lines in 44 files) into services
dropped.reason: The partial files already group by topic, and its fixes are about ordering inside one session, which one owner keeps right; a split would spread that order. Only the sandbox partials own fields of their own, if a later change needs them apart.

sections.title: CI runs
sections.text: 300 runs of the `ci` workflow from 2026-11-07 to 2026-11-22: 161 succeeded, 67 failed, 69 were cancelled. 10 of the 170 runs of `main` passed only when run again: three first attempts failed on a .NET test that then passed (one fixed since by `f535964b9`, one covered by task `6zpc`, one in F13), three on a macOS job cancelled after 15 minutes before any step ran, the others on cancelled jobs. Details in `signals/ci-runs.md`.

method.text: Three models reviewed the repository at `2a3fd8388`: Claude Opus 5.5 drove; Gemini 4 Neon and GPT 6.2 Astra analyzed. The owner asked for `antigravity-mcp:gemini-4-neon@high`, a provider this installation does not have: the same model ran through its only Antigravity provider, `antigravity-acp`. Each analyzed alone from the same brief and signals, the driver first, without reading the others. Their 21 findings were merged into `analysis/candidates.md` without authors, and each analyst tried to refute the candidates it had not raised. The driver opened the code of every finding kept here and settled each question of fact by reading or searching; no build or test was run. The owner chose to keep all 16 findings and to decide their priorities from the order of work. While landing, three numbers of this report were measured again and corrected: 13 callers of the whole-list provider save (the 14th match was the store's declaration), 36 unscaled test deadlines (not 33), and 45 fixed delays of 12.7 s in the browser test files (not 39 of 11.4 s); the defaults that F03's model-server path wrote were an implicit `api_url` of a disabled llama.cpp provider, the Codex defaults being already pruned on save.
